definition: Connectionist expert systems are artificial neural network (ANN) based expert systems where the ANN generates inferencing rules e.g., fuzzy-multi layer perceptron where linguistic and natural form of inputs are used.
details: Apart from that, rough set theory may be used for encoding knowledge in the weights better and also genetic algorithms may be used to optimize the search solutions better. Symbolic reasoning methods may also be incorporated (see hybrid intelligent system). (Also see expert system, neural network, clinical decision support system.)

explainer.lead: A connectionist expert system uses an artificial neural network as the reasoning core of an expert system. Its network generates inferencing rules, allowing designs such as fuzzy multilayer perceptrons to work with linguistic or natural-form inputs.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a helpful adviser that learns patterns in a web of tiny decision-makers instead of relying only on a handwritten list of rules. It can work with people-style descriptions such as “high” or “low,” then develop rules to help with a decision.
tiers.practitioner: Use this approach when an expert system needs ANN-generated inferencing rules or linguistic inputs, as with a fuzzy multilayer perceptron. Rough-set theory can help encode knowledge in the weights, while genetic algorithms can improve solution search; neither is required, and symbolic reasoning belongs to an optional hybrid design.
tiers.paperLevel: A connectionist expert system is an ANN-based expert system in which the ANN generates inferencing rules. A fuzzy multilayer perceptron exemplifies the approach by accepting linguistic and natural-form inputs; extensions may use rough sets for knowledge encoding in weights, genetic algorithms for search optimization, and symbolic reasoning in a hybrid intelligent system.

explainer.example: A clinical decision-support design could take a description such as “high fever,” process it with a fuzzy multilayer perceptron, and generate inferencing rules that contribute to the system’s decision support.

usedIn.name: Clinical decision support
usedIn.detail: A related setting where neural expert-system reasoning can support decisions from linguistic or natural-form inputs.

usedIn.name: Hybrid intelligent systems
usedIn.detail: Symbolic reasoning can be incorporated alongside the connectionist component.

explainer.intuition: Instead of treating an expert system only as a collection of symbolic rules, let a neural network generate the rules used for inference. Fuzzy neural designs also make room for inputs expressed in language-like terms.
howItWorks: Process them with an ANN, such as a fuzzy multilayer perceptron.
Generate inferencing rules from the network.
Optionally use rough sets for weight-based knowledge encoding and genetic algorithms for search.
Optionally add symbolic reasoning to form a hybrid intelligent system.
explainer.whyItMatters: It connects neural-network processing with expert-system inference and supports linguistic inputs. It can also be extended with rough sets, genetic algorithms, or symbolic reasoning when those additions are useful.
misconceptions: Not every neural network is a connectionist expert system: the network must serve an expert system by generating inferencing rules.
Rough sets, genetic algorithms, and symbolic reasoning are optional additions, not defining requirements.
